items.name: Nintendo Entertainment System
items.description: Nintendo's 8-bit home console family, including the regional Famicom name and compatible platform releases.

items.name: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
items.description: Nintendo's 16-bit home console family, including the regional Super Famicom name and compatible platform releases.

items.name: Nintendo 64
items.description: Nintendo’s cartridge-based 64-bit home console family, now represented by a reviewed expansion set of foundational 3D and multiplayer games.

items.name: Nintendo GameCube
items.description: Nintendo’s compact optical-disc home console family, now represented by a reviewed expansion set of platform, adventure, and multiplayer anchors.

items.name: Wii
items.description: Nintendo’s motion-focused home console family, now represented by a reviewed expansion set spanning social play, platforming, racing, and role-playing.

items.name: Wii U
items.description: Nintendo’s home console with a controller display, now represented by a reviewed expansion set of platform, racing, multiplayer, and role-playing games.

items.name: Nintendo Switch
items.description: Nintendo's hybrid home-and-portable console family; Switch Lite and the OLED model are normalized as model aliases.

items.name: Nintendo Switch 2
items.description: Nintendo’s current hybrid-console successor, represented by native Switch 2 releases with platform-specific official pages.

items.name: Game Boy family
items.description: Nintendo's original Game Boy handheld family; Pocket and Light revisions remain model aliases, while Game Boy Color has a separate platform filter for compatibility.

items.name: Game Boy Color
items.description: Nintendo’s color handheld platform with a distinct software library, now represented by a reviewed expansion set of role-playing, adventure, and platform games.

items.name: Game Boy Advance family
items.description: Nintendo's 32-bit Game Boy Advance handheld family; SP and Micro are model aliases.

items.name: Nintendo DS family
items.description: Nintendo's original dual-screen handheld family; DS Lite remains a model alias, while Nintendo DSi has a separate platform filter for DSi-specific software.

items.name: Nintendo DSi family
items.description: Nintendo’s DSi revision family, represented with an explicit DSiWare digital distribution marker rather than being conflated with DS cartridge software.

items.name: Nintendo 3DS family
items.description: Nintendo's original stereoscopic handheld family; 2DS and 3DS XL remain compatible model aliases, while New Nintendo 3DS has a separate platform filter for exclusive software.

items.name: New Nintendo 3DS family
items.description: New Nintendo 3DS revision family with a small exclusive software set; New 3DS XL and New 2DS XL remain model aliases.
